Turn a cell over

The same six sheets, but you can break them. Coarsen the units and watch which sheets stop caring. Shuffle a sheet and watch what survives — its histogram does, everything about where its values sit does not. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.

Which cell

The real tile, or one the demo model invented.

Standardized is what the model reads and writes. Physical is those same numbers unpacked, back in the units they were measured in.

1.2 km divided this many ways. 64 units is 18.8 m each; 8 units is 150 m each.

Moves that sheet's values to random spots. Its histogram cannot change. Everything about where they sit does.

what each shuffle costs

Clumping is Moran's I: does a unit resemble the ones next to it. Shuffling drops it to zero, because it is the only column here that is about where. Agreement with the other sheets is how well this sheet's values line up with the other five at the same unit — shuffling destroys that too, and no per-sheet histogram would notice.

sheetclumping nowwas agreement nowwas
What you are looking at. The real cell is the training data after standardizing. The generated cell is the model's raw output, which is already in that same space — it has not been unpacked. That is why they can share a colour scale. Switch to physical to unpack the generated one and put the real one back into measured units; the two numbers in the table below do not move, because both are scale-invariant.
Shuffle every sheet. All six histograms stay exactly as they were, and every six-number combination in the cell becomes nonsense — dense building sitting on zero roads, high shop-mix with no shops. That is what checkpoint B10b is for: per-channel marginals cannot see it.
Built by discussion/pipeline_map/gen_stack_explorer.py from the real HCMC store, pooled to 64 × 64. Values are standardized, so a colour means the same number on the real cell and the generated one.
